optimizedCv.targetRoleTitle: Product Requirements Analyst, Collaboration Software Subscriptions

professionalSummary.text: Turned weekly intake from subscription operations and customer success into user stories with acceptance criteria for self-service seat-change and invoice-download pages.
professionalSummary.witness: Turned the weekly intake from subscription operations and customer success into user stories for the self-service seat-change and invoice-download pages, each story carrying its acceptance criteria.

professionalSummary.text: Led acceptance sessions for three billing-page releases with operations analysts and a customer success manager, logging pass/fail criteria.
professionalSummary.witness: Led acceptance sessions for three billing-page releases with two operations analysts and a customer success manager, logging every criterion as passed or failed.

professionalSummary.text: Published release notes for seat-change and invoice-download pages detailing one limitation (invoices older than twelve months could not be downloaded) and support team handover requirements.
professionalSummary.witness: Published release notes for the seat-change and invoice-download pages that spelled out one limitation (invoices older than twelve months could not be downloaded) and what the support team needed to take over.

professionalSummary.text: Agreed release scope in sprint planning with engineering manager and subscription operations lead, with scope and release date determined by engineering manager.
professionalSummary.witness: Agreed release scope in sprint planning with the engineering manager and the subscription operations lead; scope and the release date were the engineering manager's call.

experienceHighlights.text: Two years on the subscription product team covering intake, story writing, acceptance sessions, and release notes for self-service billing pages.
experienceHighlights.witness: Two years on the subscription product team covering intake, story writing, acceptance sessions and release notes for the self-service billing pages.

projectsAndWorkSamples.text: Work sample includes story set for invoice-download page with acceptance criteria and pass/fail log from one acceptance session, with ticket identifiers for traceability.
projectsAndWorkSamples.witness: Work sample: the story set for the invoice-download page with its acceptance criteria, plus the pass/fail log from one acceptance session; ticket identifiers are included so the entries can be traced.

skills.text: Self-service billing page requirements gathering and documentation.
skills.witness: Two years on the subscription product team covering intake, story writing, acceptance sessions and release notes for the self-service billing pages.

optimizedCv.evidenceBoundary: The materials establish the candidate's role in writing user stories, leading acceptance sessions, publishing release notes, agreeing on scope, and the duration of their work. The materials do not establish evidence of reduced billing support tickets or the specific metric of 30 percent reduction.

decisionBoundary.statement: Qualified human review is required before any employment decision due to evidence gaps in ticket reduction metrics and unverified claims.

evidence.text: Turned the weekly intake from subscription operations and customer success into user stories for the self-service seat-change and invoice-download pages, each story carrying its acceptance criteria.
Led acceptance sessions for three billing-page releases with two operations analysts and a customer success manager, logging every criterion as passed or failed.

candidate said billing tickets 'fell by about 30 percent' after the invoice-download page launched; he said the support team had mentioned it in a stand-up and that he had not seen a ticket report himself.
evidence.notes: Unverified claim, no baseline or report.

missingEvidence: Documented reduction in billing support tickets

evidence.text: Agreed release scope in sprint planning with the engineering manager and the subscription operations lead; scope and the release date were the engineering manager's call.

Published release notes for the seat-change and invoice-download pages that spelled out one limitation (invoices older than twelve months could not be downloaded) and what the support team needed to take over.
